content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days.
- Model tends to lag in downward corrections — true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices in early days, then mean-reversion toward lower levels later.
- When sentiment history includes multiple positive spikes, model overreacts and overcorrects, leading to overshoots.
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for downward pressure.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5–7 days, apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment magnitude.
- Mean reversion is stronger in late forecast horizon — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day after day 15 if sentiment remains negative.
